operator_io_quirks: Table names with hyphens and spaces: 'current-terms', 'historical-terms', 'social-media' — must be double-quoted in generated SQL; column lookup case-insensitive.
Composite PKs: current(bioguide_id, cspan_id); current-terms(bioguide, end) — end is TEXT date-like, so PK uniqueness depends on date strings.

FK current-terms.bioguide -> current.bioguide_id: parent column is only PART of a composite PK, so it is NOT unique in the parent (541 distinct over 541 rows here, but schema does not declare it unique).
FK social-media.bioguide -> current.bioguide_id: same non-unique-parent situation; social-media.bioguide is itself PK (unique).
FK historical-terms.bioguide -> historical.bioguide_id: parent is single-column PK, unique — clean.
Self-references: none. Dangling FKs: none (all parent_exists true).

current.birthday_bio declared DATE but stored as TEXT 'YYYY-MM-DD'; historical.birthday_bio declared TEXT and also stores 'YYYY-MM-DD' — same format, different declared type, so TS dispatches Date fuzzer on current and String fuzzer on historical for the same semantic column.
current-terms.start/end, historical-terms.start/end declared TEXT but store 'YYYY-MM-DD' dates — TS will treat them as String (random charset), not Date.
current.cspan_id declared REAL, PK member, but 22% NULL — NULL PK members are allowed by sqlite here (no NOT NULL), so PK uniqueness is on (bioguide_id, cspan_id) with NULLs.
historical.thomas_id declared TEXT but stores zero-padded numeric strings '01308'; current.thomas_id declared INTEGER — same semantic column, different declared type and storage class.
historical.cspan_id, votesmart_id, maplight_id declared TEXT but store '12590.0' style float-as-text; current counterparts are REAL.
historical-terms.middle, name, relation are 100% NULL with distinct=0 — empty literal pool for those columns; TS String sampler will fall back to fresh random strings.
current.fec_id stores Python-list-repr strings "['H2OH13033', 'S6OH00163']" — not a real FK, just text; TS String sampler will contaminate these.
No NOT NULL constraints anywhere; no CHECK constraints; no UNIQUE indexes beyond PKs — TS insert failures will be rare (only PK collisions).
operator_ts_expectations: current.birthday_bio: Date fuzzer, template %Y-%m-%d (all samples match), range ~[1943,1960] from 5 sampled originals — fresh dates will be plausible but narrow; misses on queries filtering by decade/age.
current-terms.start/end, historical-terms.start/end: String fuzzer over charset a-zA-Z 0-9() — will produce garbage like 'aB3(x' instead of dates; any date comparison query will FP/FN heavily.
historical.birthday_bio: String fuzzer (declared TEXT) — same garbage-date problem, though values are dates.

current.cspan_id, govtrack_id, thomas_id, house_history_id, icpsr_id, maplight_id, votesmart_id: Number fuzzer, scale from REAL/INTEGER; range [-10^4,10^4] for REAL, [-10^4,10^4] for INTEGER — will produce negative and huge IDs unlike real 5-7 digit positive IDs; FN on range/join predicates.

current-terms.class, district, historical-terms.class, district: Number fuzzer over REAL — class will get values like -3.7 instead of {1,2,3}; district negative values; FN on 'class = 1' style filters.
social-media.facebook_id, instagram_id, twitter_id, youtube_id, govtrack: Number fuzzer over REAL — huge 15-16 digit IDs sampled from [-10^4,10^4] range, implausible; FN on equality/join.

gender_bio, party, state, type, chamber, state_rank, title, relation, religion_bio: String fuzzer with 5 sampled originals + pool — will mix real values with random charset strings; FN on 'party = Democrat' style filters, FP on LIKE.

bioguide_id / bioguide: String fuzzer, but PK — sample_fresh_primary_keys drops duplicates; FK children draw from parent's final values so joins work, but values are random charset not 'A000055' pattern; FN on 'bioguide_id LIKE A%'.
current-terms.end is PK member and TEXT date — String fuzzer produces random strings, so composite PK (bioguide, end) rarely collides; but date-range queries on end will be garbage.
Empty-pool columns (historical-terms.middle/name/relation, current-terms.last 100% NULL): String sampler with no elements -> p=1, always fresh random strings; any IS NULL query will FN.
fec_id, party_affiliations, bioguide_previous_id store list/dict reprs — String fuzzer will contaminate with random chars; queries doing LIKE '%H2%' will FP.

Number fuzzer's list_max quirk (overwrites with full-range max) means even with real elements, fresh draws span [-10^4,10^4] — implausible IDs drive FN on equality joins between current and historical on govtrack_id/thomas_id.
